title: The dream train
summary: Every night, a magical little train picks up children in pajamas and carries them gently through dreamy landscapes.

scenes.text: When the house grows quiet and the moon peeks through the window, far away you hear a soft whistle: choo-choo. It is the dream train, coming slowly along a little path of clouds. Its cars are fluffy like pillows and its lights twinkle like fireflies. The train stops beside your bed and opens its tiny door. A bear in a blue cap leans out and says, very softly, "Are you coming to dream with me?" All the children in pajamas climb aboard carefully, one behind the other, and find a warm seat by the window.

The train sets off slowly, clack-clack, and rolls into a sleeping forest. The tall trees wave their branches as if saying goodbye, and a very soft song rises from the leaves. On a round branch, big round eyes open: it is the owl. Whoo, whoo, he hoots, watching over the way. Golden fireflies drift past the window, dancing in the air. The bear hands out warm blankets and a cup of warm milk for each child. No one speaks loudly here; in the forest of dreams you only speak with your eyes and a tiny smile.

Little by little, the forest falls behind, and the train crosses a very long bridge over the sea. Below the bridge rock the soft waves. Shhh, shhh, they sing, like a lullaby made of water. Suddenly, up from the deep blue rises a huge whale. She sings a low, calm melody that tickles your heart. The moon shines on the water like a little silver path. The children rest their heads against the window and feel their eyes begin to grow heavy. The train glides so gently it seems to float over the sleeping sea.

Then the train climbs, climbs, climbs up a rainbow of night until it reaches the sky. Now it travels among a thousand stars. They shine and twinkle like little crumbs of light. Between the cars sings the wind. Cool and gentle, it ruffles the children's hair. Up here everything is calm: no hurry, no noise, only the big, quiet sky. The bear turns off the train's little lights one by one, so the night can be even sweeter. "We're almost at the land of dreams," he says, and his voice sounds like a hug.

The dream train arrives slowly at its last station, among fluffy clouds and silence. One by one, the children give a big yawn and breathe. In and out, slow and deep. The bear tucks them in with their favorite blanket and gives them a little kiss on the forehead. "Good night, little travelers," he whispers. Outside, the moon watches over them from above. And so, rocked by the gentle sway of the cars, all the children fall asleep. They smile without knowing it. Sweet dreams to you. The train will wait for you tomorrow, in the same place, when the night sings again.
